study.title: Brain Activity Associated with Expectancy-Enhanced Placebo Analgesia as Measured by Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging
study.study_design: within-subject experimental design with three sessions (two behavioral, one fMRI)
study.randomization: Subjects were randomized into two groups to receive placebo acupuncture at one of two nonacupuncture points, either sham large intestine 4 (LI 4) or sham small intestine 3 (SI 3)
study.blinding: Subjects were naive to acupuncture; sham needle was used; subjects were told the study was about acupuncture analgesia; stimulus temperature was surreptitiously decreased on placebo side during expectancy manipulation
study.population: Twenty-four right-handed healthy subjects (13 males; mean age, 28.4 years ± 6.6 SD) who were naive to acupuncture
study.disease_condition: healthy volunteers; experimentally induced thermal pain
study.inclusion_criteria: right-handed healthy subjects; naive to acupuncture; able to reliably distinguish high pain intensity stimuli from low pain intensity stimuli
study.exclusion_criteria: subjects whose subjective pain ratings did not clearly correspond to the magnitude of the stimulus intensity (i.e., the average rating of high pain stimuli was not higher than that of low pain stimuli in each RS); incomplete fMRI data sets

arms.dropouts: not_reported at arm level; 8 of 24 total were dropped (5 could not reliably distinguish pain intensities; 3 had incomplete fMRI data)

extraction_notes.note: Table 3 in the paper is labeled 'Brain areas activated during the comparison of fMRI signal change differences (after treatment > before treatment) between both placebo and control sides.' The text references 'Table 3' when discussing pretreatment baseline rating differences for low pain across sides, which appears to be an error in the paper — the relevant data is in Table 2. Extracted faithfully as described.

In Table 4 (correlation analysis), the Right fusiform gyrus (37) peak coordinate is listed as −50, −48, −20, which is a negative x-coordinate (left hemisphere by MNI convention) despite being labeled 'Right.' This discrepancy is preserved exactly as reported in the paper. The paper labels it 'Right fusiform gyrus' in the text.

The paper states the figure panel B shows activation at 'right anterior insula (46, 20, −4)' which matches Table 3. The paper uses the notation '46, 20, 4' in the figure caption text. From context the z-coordinate is −4 as shown in Table 3. Extracted as −4 from Table 3.

In Table 5 (post-treatment high pain), two rows for 'Right inferior parietal cortex (40)' appear with different coordinates (56, −50, 32; cluster 766) and (62, −30, 50; cluster 263). These are separate clusters and were extracted as separate entries.

The paper references a supplemental Figure 1 (supplemental Fig. 1, available at www.jneurosci.org as supplemental material) showing experimental procedures. This supplement was not provided in the PDF and no additional data were extractable from it.

Deqi sensations were not formally assessed or reported in this study. The paper does not include any deqi questionnaire, MASS, or similar sensory outcome. Subjects were naive to acupuncture and the sham needle does not penetrate skin.

Blinding success (participant guessing of allocation) was not formally assessed. The paper describes expectancy manipulation but does not report whether subjects correctly identified which side was treated.
No adverse events section was included in the paper. It is not reported whether adverse events occurred or were monitored.

The paper does not report individual-level stimulus temperatures used for low and high pain conditions; only the range selection criteria are described (low pain: 8–11 on 0–20 Sensory Box; high pain: 14–17). Temperatures were individually calibrated per subject.

The paper describes two ANOVA analyses on pain ratings. The primary ANOVA compares pre-post difference on placebo vs control (p < 0.0001). A second ANOVA confirms no high vs low pain interaction in this difference (p < 0.26). The first ANOVA also confirms high > low pain at pretreatment (p < 0.0001). These are extracted as separate outcome entries.
The correlation analysis r-scores reported in Table 4 are described as 'r score of peak voxel.' These are peak voxel correlations, not cluster-level correlations, and are extracted as reported.

The arms in this study are within-subject conditions (placebo side vs control side), not between-subject groups. The 'arm' structure was used to capture this distinction for extraction purposes, but both 'arms' involved all 16 subjects.

In Table 5, the cluster size for 'Right superior frontal gyrus (10)' is listed as '95' in one column and '3.39' in another, but looking at the table formatting, the cluster size appears as 95 and Z score 3.39. The coordinate 4, 68, 16 is listed. Extracted as reported.

In Table 5, 'Left inferior frontal gyrus (44)' and 'Left inferior frontal gyrus (47)' have cluster sizes listed in what appears to be the Z score column (23 and 50 respectively) and Z scores in adjacent columns (3.05 and 3.04). Given table formatting, cluster sizes are 23 and 50 voxels, Z scores are 3.05 and 3.04. Extracted accordingly.

Some minus signs in coordinates (e.g., negative z-values) may have been rendered inconsistently in the PDF text (e.g., as long dashes vs hyphens). All coordinates were verified against table context and negative signs preserved.
